stories.title: AI spending fears deepen the global tech selloff
stories.dek: AI-spending jitters drove a broad tech-led selloff, with US indexes sharply lower in early trading.
body: European shares fell as renewed concern about returns on heavy AI investment weighed on technology stocks. The STOXX 600 was down around 0.3% in morning trading, though it remained on track for a monthly gain.
US futures also pointed lower, with S&P 500 e-minis down 0.89% in Reuters’ morning report. After the open, the S&P 500 fell 1.16% and the Nasdaq dropped 2.26%, while the Dow edged up 0.08%.

sources.title: Tech giants' spending spooks investors as bonds rally
Nasdaq tumbles at open as Amazon, Intel add to AI spending woes

stories.title: Euro-zone growth beats forecasts as inflation risks persist
stories.dek: The bloc’s growth beat expectations, but uneven national results and rising price pressures cloud the policy picture.
body: Euro-zone GDP grew 0.4% quarter on quarter in the third quarter, slowing from 0.6% in the previous quarter but exceeding the 0.2% growth economists had forecast.

Germany expanded 0.2%, Spain and the Netherlands each grew 0.6%, Italy was flat and France contracted 0.1%. Separate national inflation readings showed price growth accelerating in several major euro-zone economies, complicating the outlook for the ECB.

sources.title: Euro zone growth beats projections again

stories.title: German inflation cools more than expected
stories.dek: A larger-than-expected slowdown in German prices offered some relief amid wider euro-area inflation concerns.
body: Germany’s harmonised inflation rate slowed to 2.8% year on year in October, from 3.3% in September and below the 3.1% expected by economists polled by Reuters.
The first month of a fuel-tax cut helped ease pump-price pressures. Core inflation also declined, to 2.1% from 2.4%.

sources.title: German inflation slows more than expected in October

stories.title: ECB survey finds more euro-zone firms anticipate wage pressure
stories.dek: The survey adds to the ECB’s focus on whether the energy-driven inflation rise will feed into wages.
body: The ECB’s quarterly survey of large euro-zone companies found that 40% expected or saw a risk of higher wage demands, up from 20% in the previous survey in July.

Companies still expected wage growth to slow, from 3.2% last year to 3.0% this year and 2.9% next year, but at a more gradual pace than previously anticipated. The survey also pointed to continued cost pressures, including from energy and agricultural prices.

sources.title: Euro zone companies brace for higher wage demands, ECB poll shows

stories.title: US labour costs rise at a slower pace in the third quarter
stories.dek: A moderation in quarterly labour-cost growth offered a counterpoint to recent US inflation concerns.
body: US employment costs rose 0.8% in the third quarter, matching economists’ expectations but slowing from a 0.9% increase in the second quarter, according to the Employment Cost Index.
Wages and salaries rose 0.7% in the quarter, also slower than the prior period. Total labour costs were up 3.4% over the year to September, while inflation-adjusted wages fell 0.6%.

sources.title: Slower wage growth curbs US labor costs in third quarter

stories.title: BP posts $8.46 billion quarterly profit and reaches debt target early
stories.dek: Higher energy prices and refining margins lifted BP’s profit to a record under its current reporting measure.
body: BP reported third-quarter underlying replacement-cost profit of $8.46 billion, above the $7.33 billion expected by analysts and up from $2.2 billion a year earlier. The company said its quarterly operating cash flow was $14.8 billion.

Net debt fell to $13.9 billion, allowing BP to reach its net-debt target a year early. The company said it would use the windfall to settle its remaining Deepwater Horizon liabilities; its shares were up about 0.5% in morning trading.

sources.title: BP beats third-quarter forecasts with record $8.46 billion profit

stories.title: Sanofi lifts its 2026 outlook again as quarterly profit beats forecasts
stories.dek: A strong quarter and upgraded guidance lifted the French drugmaker’s shares, while its new CEO flagged dealmaking ambitions.
body: Sanofi raised its 2026 targets for the second time this year, projecting low-teens sales growth and mid-teens growth in business earnings per share at constant exchange rates.

Third-quarter business operating income was €5.43 billion, ahead of the €4.32 billion analyst consensus cited by Reuters. The French drugmaker’s shares rose nearly 6% to their highest level since April as it also signalled interest in acquisitions to replenish its pipeline.

stories.title: Puma gains as results point to progress in its turnaround
stories.dek: Quarterly results and its product rollout helped the sportswear group stand out in a weak European market.
body: Puma shares advanced after the German sportswear company reported third-quarter sales that Reuters said were in line with estimates, supporting signs of progress in its turnaround.
Reuters’ European-market report put the shares up 4% in one update; a later market report recorded a gain of 6.9%.

stories.title: Bayer rises after winning Roundup cancer-claims trial
stories.dek: A courtroom win gave Bayer a lift amid its long-running Roundup litigation overhang.
body: Bayer rose after winning a trial on Thursday involving claims by three women that its Roundup weedkiller caused their cancer. Reuters reported the shares up 4.1% in European trading.
The court outcome offered a positive legal development for the company as investors weighed ongoing litigation exposure.

stories.title: Binance says partners have located about $3 billion in affected assets
stories.dek: Asset freezes covered roughly half the reported haul, but crypto prices remained under pressure as the recovery picture stayed incomplete.
body: Following the reported Binance security incident, the exchange said it and its partners had located about $3 billion of the estimated $6.3 billion in affected assets; Reuters reported that it gave no update on the remaining $3.3 billion.

Bitcoin reached a six-week low and was last down about 3% in Reuters’ market update, while ether was down more than 3%. Reuters also reported that stablecoin issuers had frozen roughly half of the stolen assets.

sources.title: Analysts react as Binance freezes assets after $6.3 billion security breach

stories.title: Intel sinks about a quarter as a PC slump and weak outlook overshadow AI growth
stories.dek: Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $15–16bn came in well below the roughly $17.1bn analysts expected.
body: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15bn–$16bn, below both the third quarter’s $16.5bn and the consensus of about $17.1bn. It expects adjusted gross margin to fall to 38% from 44.1%, and adjusted EPS of about $0.25 against roughly $0.43 expected.

PC revenue fell 5% to $8.1bn while data-centre and AI revenue rose 78%. Management said PC weakness would last at least through the first half of next year, and also pointed to a factory accident in Israel.
The shares were down about 25% before the US open, dragging chipmakers in Asia and Europe lower.

stories.title: Amazon misses on earnings as AI spending pushes free cash flow negative
stories.dek: AWS grew 39%, but trailing free cash flow swung to about minus $42.4bn.
body: Third-quarter sales rose 12% to $201.9bn and AWS grew 39%, but earnings per share of $1.89 missed the $1.96 estimate and sales were slightly light.
Trailing twelve-month free cash flow turned negative at about −$42.4bn as Amazon lifted its 2026 capital spending plan to around $220bn, much of it on AI infrastructure.
The shares fell about 7% before the open, feeding the wider debate over whether AI capex is earning a return.

stories.title: Binance hit by an estimated $6.3bn hack, likely crypto’s largest theft
stories.dek: About $3bn has been frozen; Binance says it will cover all losses and reopen withdrawals within two days.
body: Binance halted withdrawals after attackers drained an estimated $6.3bn. Around $3bn has been frozen with blockchain partners and law enforcement, and investigators have linked the attack to North Korea.
The exchange first pointed to a compromised employee laptop, then said it had found further points of breach. It has set aside about $6.34bn to make customers whole and says deposits were unaffected.
Bitcoin dropped below $77,000 and ether fell nearly 6%, with roughly $1.5bn of leveraged positions liquidated.

stories.title: Brent climbs toward $118 as tanker attacks keep Hormuz risk alive
stories.dek: Iran claimed mine strikes on commercial vessels even as Washington said the war would end soon.
body: Brent rose about 2.5% to near $117.80 a barrel and WTI to about $104 after reports of attacks on tankers and Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi Arabia.
President Trump said the conflict with Iran would end soon without saying how, while US Central Command said southern shipping lanes were open. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran.
Traders are also weighing the risk of renewed fighting around the 3 November US midterm elections.

stories.title: AstraZeneca beats third-quarter forecasts and keeps full-year guidance
stories.dek: Pre-tax profit rose 22% to $3.96bn on revenue of $16.21bn.
body: Revenue rose 6.7% to $16.21bn and pre-tax profit climbed 22% to $3.96bn, both ahead of market expectations. Full-year guidance was unchanged.
The shares rose almost 4%, one of the main supports for the FTSE 100 on a weak day for growth stocks elsewhere.

stories.title: NatWest falls 7% as net interest income misses and AI-led job cuts reach 1,400
stories.dek: Attributable profit slipped 4.1% to £1.53bn; the full-year outlook was kept.
body: Net interest income rose 8.9% to £3.56bn but missed analyst forecasts, and profit attributable to shareholders fell 4.1% to £1.53bn.
The bank said about 1,400 roles have gone this year, around 1,000 of them in the quarter, as AI changes how it operates. Its full-year outlook was reaffirmed.
NatWest was the biggest drag on the FTSE 100 by midday.

stories.title: Mobico agrees £308m cash takeover by Leita Mobility at a 55% premium
stories.dek: The 46p-a-share offer values the bus and coach operator at about £2.32bn including debt.
body: Mobico backed a cash offer of 46p a share from Leita Mobility, part of Spain’s Autobuses de León, a 55% premium to the 20 October close of 29.7p.
Including debt, the deal values the group at around £2.32bn. It is expected to complete through a court-sanctioned scheme. The shares rose about 12%.

stories.title: Sandisk falls despite a revenue beat and an eight-for-one split
stories.dek: Investors worry memory pricing is close to a peak.
body: Fiscal first-quarter revenue rose 23% to $11.03bn, above the company’s own forecast, and Sandisk announced an eight-for-one stock split.
The shares still fell nearly 8% before the open as investors questioned how long strong memory prices can last.

body: Third-quarter GDP beat the 3.2% estimate. Core PCE rose 0.3% in September, below the 0.4% forecast, for 3.1% year on year, while headline PCE ran at 3.6%. Weekly jobless claims fell to 194,000.

stories.title: Fed holds rates at 3.75%–4% as two officials vote for a hike
stories.dek: Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favour of tightening.
body: The Federal Reserve under Chair Kevin Warsh left its target range at 3.75%–4%, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voting for an increase. After the press conference, futures priced a December hike at close to 90%.
